text:
jamie: FYI team — we just got a report from a partner that one of their developer portal logs included an old OAuth client secret we use for the `partner-bridge` integration. Partner claims it was posted by mistake in a public gist. Treat as compromised and rotate ASAP.

maria: ack. thanks for flagging. do we have the client id? which envs are affected?

jamie: client_id: abc123-partner. Looks like only the integration for the non-production org (staging) used that secret, but we need to assume worst-case until we confirm.

sam: I'm taking ownership of rotation. Plan: 1) disable current secret in Okta 2) generate new secret 3) update infra secrets in Vault and redeploy connectors 4) audit tokens and sessions. ETA 40m.

alex: tagging platform owners — after rotation we should do a short rollback window to validate 3rd-party behavior. Also will need a short maintenance window announced to the partner and internal support.

priya: I'll prepare a consolidated incident note for customer-facing channels and the partner comms template. Do we want to block staging traffic while we rotate?

sam: yes, block inbound traffic from that partner's client_id to staging until new secret is live. I'll add a temporary rule in our API gateway (WAF).

maria: checklist for rotation (minimal):
- Revoke current secret in Okta/admin console
- Reissue client secret and paste into internal Vault path `secret/integrations/partner-bridge`
- Restart connector service: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/partner-bridge -n infra`
- Revoke any active refresh tokens tied to that client_id (script below)

sec-bot: automated note: a new Okta app credential can be created via API. Example:
```
POST /api/v1/apps/{appId}/credentials/keys
Authorization: SSWS ${OKTA_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "validityYears": 1
}
```

jamie: sam — please paste the Vault path and the exact Vault write command you will use when ready so ops can follow. Priya — ping support and partner with a 30m heads-up once we schedule the brief maintenance.

sam: writing to Vault path: `secret/integrations/partner-bridge`
Command: `vault kv put secret/integrations/partner-bridge client_id=abc123-partner client_secret=new_secret_value`

sam: also running token revocation for refresh tokens: `python tools/revoke_refresh_tokens.py --client-id abc123-partner --env staging`

priya: prepping message now. draft snippet: "We're rotating the staging OAuth secret used by partner integrations due to a suspected exposure. There will be a brief interruption (estimated <10 minutes) while we apply the update. No production traffic is affected."

maria: after rotation, run these audits and drop logs here:
- List of IPs that used the client_id in the last 30 days (`/logs/query`)
- Any token exchange events from suspicious geos
- Access logs for service accounts associated with connector

alex: note for follow-up: implement CI check to block secrets in public gists for repos that reference partner client_ids (simple regex + GitHub webhook). Put PR in backlog.

jamie: final items: assign post-mortem if partner confirms gist was public and secret used externally. Sam, update this thread when rotation complete and paste Okta revocation id. Priya, send partner note once we finish.

sam: started rotation now. disabling old secret in Okta -> done (okta_revocation_id: okta-revoke-2026-09-21-01). writing new secret to Vault -> done. restarted connector -> rollout succeeded. revoking refresh tokens -> script returned 12 tokens revoked.

priya: partner notified. support notified. message to partner: sent and acknowledged.

maria: running post-rotation audits now. pulling logs, will post any anomalies in 30m.

jamie: great work team. closing this as "actioned" for now. we'll reconvene if Maria finds anything suspicious. :thumbsup:
